title: Ellington's life on the road and Jones's own restlessness
summary: Willard and Jones consider that the road kept Ellington going; Jones likes new places but needs a push to travel.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: He worked very hard at it. I don't know whether I could stand to be out on the road that long.
Oh, but he survived on it. I mean most people couldn't stand it, but he needed it. I mean he had to keep moving.
Yeah, that's right. I think so. It kept his momentum up, you know. And he loved to be around people.
And different people all the time. He had to have the people around him changing all the time, for stimulation.

Well, I like that. I like that. But I just have to get somebody to push me out there. I'm quite lazy about it. But I like that. I get excited when I go to different countries and different places, different musicians, fresh ideas. And hearing new things and all that. That keeps me going. Because when I get around the house sometimes I say, 'Gee whiz, what can I do today that's worthwhile?'
